label: June 2026 paper — gap-fill practice variants (booklet Q1–Q50)

items.stem: Let y₁ = β₁ + β₂ + u₁; y₂ = 2β₁ + u₂; y₃ = β₁ − β₂ + u₃ with uncorrelated errors of variance σ². The best linear unbiased estimator of β₁ is
items.explanation: By the Gauss–Markov theorem the BLUE is the OLS estimator b = (X′X)⁻¹X′y with design matrix X = [[1, 1], [2, 0], [1, −1]]. Here X′X = [[6, 0], [0, 2]], and the row of (X′X)⁻¹X′ for β₁ gives (y₁ + 2y₂ + y₃)/6. Trap: X′y without (X′X)⁻¹ is not unbiased, and the other row estimates the other coefficient.

items.stem: Let y₁ = β₁ + 2β₂ + u₁; y₂ = β₁ + u₂; y₃ = β₁ − 2β₂ + u₃ with uncorrelated errors of variance σ². The best linear unbiased estimator of β₂ is
items.explanation: By the Gauss–Markov theorem the BLUE is the OLS estimator b = (X′X)⁻¹X′y with design matrix X = [[1, 2], [1, 0], [1, −2]]. Here X′X = [[3, 0], [0, 8]], and the row of (X′X)⁻¹X′ for β₂ gives (y₁ − y₃)/4. Trap: X′y without (X′X)⁻¹ is not unbiased, and the other row estimates the other coefficient.

items.stem: Let y₁ = β₁ + β₂ + u₁; y₂ = β₁ − β₂ + u₂; y₃ = 2β₁ + u₃ with uncorrelated errors of variance σ². The best linear unbiased estimator of β₁ is
items.explanation: By the Gauss–Markov theorem the BLUE is the OLS estimator b = (X′X)⁻¹X′y with design matrix X = [[1, 1], [1, −1], [2, 0]]. Here X′X = [[6, 0], [0, 2]], and the row of (X′X)⁻¹X′ for β₁ gives (y₁ + y₂ + 2y₃)/6. Trap: X′y without (X′X)⁻¹ is not unbiased, and the other row estimates the other coefficient.

items.stem: Let y₁ = 2β₁ + β₂ + u₁; y₂ = β₂ + u₂; y₃ = β₁ − 2β₂ + u₃ with uncorrelated errors of variance σ². The best linear unbiased estimator of β₂ is
items.explanation: By the Gauss–Markov theorem the BLUE is the OLS estimator b = (X′X)⁻¹X′y with design matrix X = [[2, 1], [0, 1], [1, −2]]. Here X′X = [[5, 0], [0, 6]], and the row of (X′X)⁻¹X′ for β₂ gives (y₁ + y₂ − 2y₃)/6. Trap: X′y without (X′X)⁻¹ is not unbiased, and the other row estimates the other coefficient.

items.stem: Which of the following is not a consequence of heteroscedastic errors on ordinary least squares estimation?
options: The usual OLS standard errors are biased
OLS estimates of β are biased
Tests based on the usual t and F statistics are unreliable
items.explanation: With heteroscedasticity OLS stays unbiased (E(u) = 0 is all unbiasedness needs) but loses efficiency, and the usual variance formula σ²(X′X)⁻¹ is wrong. So 'OLS estimates of β are biased' is the one that does not follow. Trap: unbiasedness needs only E(u | X) = 0; most violations damage efficiency or standard errors instead.

items.stem: Which of the following is not a consequence of positively autocorrelated errors on ordinary least squares estimation?
options: The usual OLS standard errors are understated
OLS estimates of β are biased (with fixed regressors)
The Durbin–Watson statistic tends to be below 2
items.explanation: Autocorrelation leaves OLS unbiased when the regressors are fixed, but it is inefficient and the conventional standard errors are too small. So 'OLS estimates of β are biased (with fixed regressors)' is the one that does not follow. Trap: unbiasedness needs only E(u | X) = 0; most violations damage efficiency or standard errors instead.

items.stem: Which of the following is not a consequence of perfect multicollinearity on ordinary least squares estimation?
options: The individual coefficients cannot be estimated uniquely
Some linear combinations of β are still estimable
The fitted values ŷ cannot be computed
items.explanation: With an exact linear dependence (X′X)⁻¹ does not exist, so individual β's are not identified, yet the projection of y on the column space — the fitted values — is still unique. So 'The fitted values ŷ cannot be computed' is the one that does not follow. Trap: unbiasedness needs only E(u | X) = 0; most violations damage efficiency or standard errors instead.

items.stem: Which of the following is not a consequence of omitting a relevant regressor correlated with the included ones on ordinary least squares estimation?
items.explanation: The omitted variable's effect is absorbed by the included regressors it is correlated with: E(b₁) = β₁ + (X₁′X₁)⁻¹X₁′X₂β₂ ≠ β₁. So 'The included coefficients remain unbiased' is the one that does not follow. Trap: unbiasedness needs only E(u | X) = 0; most violations damage efficiency or standard errors instead.

items.stem: Which of the following is not a consequence of including an irrelevant regressor on ordinary least squares estimation?
options: Some degrees of freedom are lost
items.explanation: An extra regressor with true coefficient 0 keeps OLS unbiased; the cost is precision (larger variances) and degrees of freedom. So 'The coefficient estimates become biased' is the one that does not follow. Trap: unbiasedness needs only E(u | X) = 0; most violations damage efficiency or standard errors instead.

items.stem: Which of the following is not a consequence of classical measurement error in a regressor on ordinary least squares estimation?
options: The slope estimate is biased towards zero
The bias does not vanish as n grows
items.explanation: Noise in x makes the regressor correlated with the composite error, so b is attenuated: plim b = β·Var(x*)/(Var(x*) + Var(noise)). So 'The slope estimate is unbiased' is the one that does not follow. Trap: unbiasedness needs only E(u | X) = 0; most violations damage efficiency or standard errors instead.
